To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the person-to person genomic variability is a strong predictor of drug safety and that the deleterious effect of nonsynonymous variants in drug related proteins can be used as a novel measure of drug safety.
the genome sequence variability predicts drug withdrawals and precautions.

the person-to- person genome sequence variability is an independent predictor of drug safety and that the deleterious impact on structure and function predicted by the Sift algorithm for 2504 individuals is a strong predictor of drug withdrawal from the market and precautionary drug use.
In summary, our research is concerned with
drug withdrawals and precautions from the market, and their relationship with genome sequence variability.
the development of novel methods for the evaluation of drug safety and the identification of novel biomarkers for the prediction of drug withdrawals and drug precautions.
the development of novel methods for predicting drug safety and efficacy, based on personal genome analysis, and for identifying the genetic basis of drug response variability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the deleterious impact (i.e. the deleterious effect) of a drug on a person depends on the genetic makeup of that person, and the deleterious effects of a drug on different persons depend on their genetic makeup.

the deleterious impact on drug-related proteins of the genome sequence variability predicted by the SIFTSIFT algorithm is significantly lower for withdrawn and precautionary drugs compared to other drugs.
a drug with a higher genomic deleterious score is more likely to be withdrawn from the market, and a drug with a lower deleterious score has less potential to be withdrawn from market.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genome sequence variability is predictive of the risk of adverse drug effects.
the genomic deleterious impact (i.e., the number of nonsynonymous variants) on drug-related proteins is an independent predictor of drug withdrawal and precaution.
drug-related protein sequence variability predicts the safety of the drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the genome sequence of an individual may be used as a predictive biomarker for drug withdrawals and precautions.
the person-to person genome variability is a strong predictor of drug withdrawals.
the person-to person genomic sequence variability is a major determinant of the safety of a drug, and that it is important to take it into consideration during the drug development process.
